viewer_sees: The twin brothers stand side by side on a ballcourt at dusk, ball in hand, facing a black cleft in the ground at the right from which owls spill into the air
The Guatemalan highlands of the K’iche’ Maya: volcano, lake, mist, a village of thatched houses around a ceiba tree
In 1701 a friar copies the old text by candlelight in a stone cell, the worn older pages beside him

PROCESS CUTAWAY: a cross-section of the earth: two brothers play ball on a sunlit court above; below, in a dark hall under the same court, the lords of Xibalba look up as dust trickles from the ceiling
Owls lead two brothers down a steep stair toward a river of red water that they cross
In the dim hall two brothers bow to two carved wooden figures seated in the seats of honor while the real lords watch from the shadows
The lords laugh, then point to a stone bench that is glowing red like coals; the two brothers hesitate
Two brothers sit back to back in a pitch-black chamber, each with a lit torch and a lit cigar, as a stone door closes
EMPTY AFTERMATH: two burnt-out stubs of torch and cigar on a stone floor at dawn; the camera rises out through the door to a ballcourt where a last paving stone is set over a grave
A bare calabash tree with one calm pale head resting in its fork, new round fruit swelling on every branch
A young woman reaches up toward the head in the tree; a glowing drop lands in her open palm
The twins play ball in the court; the ground shakes, dust sifts, owls burst out of cracks in the stone
PROCESS CUTAWAY: a hawk drawn like an anatomical plate, inside it a snake, inside that a toad, inside that one louse glowing as the message
The twins plant two green canes in the packed earth floor in the middle of their grandmother’s house while she watches from the hearth
BEFORE / AFTER diptych: left half the two canes dry and brown, right half the same two canes green and sprouting
The twins cross a river by walking on their blowguns laid like a bridge, a single mosquito glint flying ahead of them
A row of lords in the dim hall each flinch and cry out in turn, mouths wide and hands slapping at their necks, one tiny mosquito glint streaking along the row
The twins greet each lord by name and step around the glowing bench; as they pass, the hall torches gutter and night falls over Xibalba
In the House of Darkness the twins light the lords’ torch with red macaw feathers and their cigars with fireflies, and every one comes through unburned
In a hail-swept stone chamber the twins sit unshivering while two jaguars gnaw bones thrown to them
Bats whirl in the dark; Hunahpu peers out of his blowgun to look for dawn as a huge winged shadow sweeps across
Animals of every kind stream across the floor toward Xbalanque; a turtle steps forward from the swarm
The lords play with a pale round head as a ball; a rabbit bursts loose from beside Xbalanque
The lords chase the rabbit while Xbalanque swaps the heads back; the twins glance at a far oven glowing
The twins whisper to two soothsayers beside a grinding stone, telling them how to answer the lords
The lords stoke a huge oven pit; the twins embrace and leap into the flames
The lords scatter ground ash into the river; underwater the ash sinks and on the fifth day two fish-men rise
Two ragged wanderers dance before the lords; a small thatched house bursts into flame and then stands whole
One wanderer falls under a cloth, the other waves a hand and he rises; the lords laugh and clap
The lords step forward eagerly; the twins strike the two chief lords, who collapse in dust, and the other lords recoil
The twins honor their father on a temple platform at first light, then rise into the sky above the temple city as two lights, one blazing gold and one pale silver: the sun and the moon

A Classic Maya painted vase turns slowly in a lamplit study with figures that may be the twins; the camera closes on the twin figures, then pulls back to an old manuscript and two scholars pointing at different lines
A long stone shelf: burnt stubs of the father, then the macaw torch and firefly cigar, then two green canes sprouting through ash
The lords lean forward in their seats, rapt, applauding the show
The rubber ball rests alone on the ballcourt floor at dusk, a long way down
End card: poster of the whole story with the title, the twins, the lords and the SUBSCRIBE button
